subject: Private Offer — term flexibility request and buyer approval chain
messages:
From: Sarah Dunne <sarah.dunne@heliotech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement here has a couple of asks before we can proceed with a private offer:

- Our finance team prefers a 9-month engagement (mid-year budget cycles) rather than the standard 12 months. Is that possible on the AWS Private Offer path?
- We have multiple BU approvers — procurement@heliotech.com, legal, and the CFO. Can you map the approval chain so we know who needs to sign in which order?

I've attached our SOW for context.

Best,
Sarah

[attachment: HelioTech_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 242KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Sarah Dunne <sarah.dunne@heliotech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the SOW. Quick answers up front:

- Short answer: yes, we can do a 9-month private offer, but that will require an exception on the PO duration (AWS marketplace supports 1–36 month private offers technically, but our standard play is 12/24).
- Approval chain: procurement -> legal review -> CFO signoff (finance) -> marketplace activation. I'll map this with internal ops and confirm gating windows.

@Vanessa / @Ben / @Karthik / @Soojin — can we triage a one-time duration exception and pricing impact? I'd like to propose a pro‑rated upfront commit for 9 months (60% of annualized commit) to keep unit economics aligned. Also need SOC2 evidence and the standard evidence pack for activation.

Sarah — attaching a draft of the terms I'll propose internally. Expect an internal update by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.example.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

[attachment: HLT-1274-proposed-po-terms.pdf (PDF, 68KB)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Marissa — thanks for looping us in. High-level:

- I support a 9-month duration if finance gets comfortable with the upfront structure. We should avoid pricing concessions that set a precedent.
- Suggested cadence: 60% upfront based on annualized commit, remainder invoiced month-by-month (net 30). That preserves ARR/run-rate while matching HelioTech's capex cycle.
- We need explicit CFO approval to accept the shorter term; can we get HelioTech to confirm the CFO will sign (not just procurement)? If they need alternative signature routing we can accept procurement + legal with a CFO notification step, but our STIR (activation) requires CFO signoff for under-12-month exceptions.

If Ben can model the margin impact with those parameters, I'll OK the exception and we can draft the private offer.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Sales Director | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Quick finance read:

- 9-month duration at a prorated commit with 60% upfront vs annualized baseline reduces our recognized ARR by ~25% in year 1 but keeps cashflow upfront if they accept the upfront.
- Pricing: to hold unit economics we should keep list price, apply no more than a 10% discount on the annualized equivalent. If they require a larger concession, we should ask for an expanded onboarding fee or pilot add-on to justify.

Numbers attached (simple model). If HelioTech will do 60% upfront we can absorb a 6% one-time term-exception discount and still hit margin targets.

-Ben
[attachment: HLT-1274-finance-model.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Operational notes for marketplace activation and approvals:

- AWS MPO supports 1–36 month terms but Marketplace ops will flag non-standard durations for manual activation. Expect a 3–5 business day activation window once documents are signed and the HubSpot/PO payload is submitted.
- Required evidence: SOC2 report, company registration, technical contact, and billing contact. We already have SOC2 on S3: s3://redwood-evidence/heliotech/soc2-report-2026.pdf — please confirm HelioTech has required procurement metadata (PO number, buyer email) in the DocuSign envelope so AWS can map accounts.
- Approval chain note: if HelioTech's CFO signs, AWS will accept the private offer immediately on submit. If only procurement signs, AWS may require a buyer escalation step which can add 48–72 hours. Recommend we get explicit CFO sign-off.

-Karthik
Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Sarah Dunne <sarah.dunne@heliotech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question — can we do 9 months instead of 12?

Thanks, all — Sarah, consolidating next steps and the plan so HelioTech has a single path forward: 

1) Term & pricing: Redwood can offer a 9-month private offer under deal HLT-1274 with a 60% upfront commit (annualized basis) and a one-time term-exception discount of 6% on the annualized price to align economics.
2) Signatures & approvals: procurement + legal can start the DocuSign envelope, but we need explicit CFO sign-off on the envelope for fastest marketplace activation. If HelioTech's CFO cannot sign, expect a 48–72 hour additional AWS validation step.
3) Evidence for activation: please upload/confirm SOC2 to the DocuSign/HubSpot record (we've linked our copy here for reference). AWS will require the SOC2 file and PO metadata.
4) Timeline: once signed with CFO included, predicted activation = 3–5 business days. If only procurement signs, predicted activation = 5–8 business days.

If you confirm the CFO will sign, I'll prepare the private offer payload and send a DocuSign link this afternoon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
